title: He just gets up and he goes: I'm gonna go again
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When a bold bid fails, what do you do the next morning?

As I retell the chapter, the author offered the other side's shareholders a large number of notes that paid far more than their dividends. I said: the notes are a piece of paper that says, you are going to get this interest further down the road. He would pay them off from the company's profits and by selling parts of the company.
It didn't work. Another buyer came in. The author realized his bid was a long shot, I said, but so was everything else in his career.

A student said: I think he was kind of on to the next. If something doesn't work out, he goes to the next thing. I said: he is very resilient. What is amazing is that he just gets up and goes: I'm just gonna go again.

groups.heading: I need to make more money so I can play with the big boys

lines.text: But what is interesting, I said, is that right away he goes into: I need to make more money so that I can play with the big boys. So how does he make money? From programming content. He goes: this will allow me to make more money and grow. And eventually I'm going to go for the networks.
Immediately he goes into: what can I do to increase my revenue, I said.

groups.heading: I would never take the risk that he's taking

lines.text: We want to read a balance sheet, I said, because we want to know how much he is leveraging. He is a little crazy with leveraging. I would never take the risk that he is taking. I think he takes on way too much debt.

It is amazing that he has that tolerance for risk, I said. Everybody has a different threshold for risk. Reading the balance sheet will give us a good indication of how leveraged certain companies are.
I said to look at how conservative the balance sheet is, and how many years the company has consistently paid dividends. All of those things are important.
What is your threshold for risk?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a bold bid or plan of yours that failed.
Write what you did the next morning.
Write how you will raise your revenue next.
Write the debt you carry and how conservative your balance sheet is.
Write your threshold for risk, and whether my view or the author's is closer to yours.

check.q: What did I say about the author after the bid failed?
choices: He just gets up and goes again

check.q: What did I say about the author's debt?
choices: He takes on way too much debt, and I would never take that risk

check.q: What did I say everybody has?

recap: After a failed bid, get up and go again, and know your own threshold for risk.
